method: Personal bank wire (SWIFT) via BOC e-banking
eligibility: Any individual; funds already in own CNY account
pros: Official channel, tracked, no approval needed up to US$50,000/day on ID documents
cons: FX spread ~0.21% + wire 1‰ (¥50-¥260) + ¥150 cable; possible OUR surcharge; US FBAR/8938 if applicable
conversion_penalty_anatomy: China: no FX tax on conversion; FX spread + wire tariff. US: §988 gain/loss, FBAR >$10k, Form 8938 thresholds

eligibility: Ask the BOC branch whether personal OUR is offered; corporate tariff lists US$15 (BOC NY) / US$25 (other US banks)
pros: Recipient receives the full amount; intermediate fees borne by sender
cons: Surcharge US$15-$25 per wire on top of M01; personal applicability not expressly stated by BOC
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Same as M01 plus the OUR surcharge

eligibility: UnionPay debit card; ≤¥100,000/card/year; ≤US$10,000 cash per person without declaration
pros: No correspondent chain; USD in hand at destination
cons: ATM fee ¥12+1% (max ¥112); cash exchange price differs from spot; >$10,000 border declaration; loss/theft risk
conversion_penalty_anatomy: ATM fee + cash FX spread; >$10k undeclared = CBP/FinCEN 105 violation

method: Overseas ATM withdrawal on a CNY card
eligibility: UnionPay debit card with CNY balance; Mastercard/Visa cards cost more
pros: Available worldwide without any approval
cons: UnionPay ¥12+1% (max ¥112/tx); MC/Visa 2.5% ($3-$40) from 2026-11-11; daily limits; DCC risk
conversion_penalty_anatomy: ATM fee only (no FX conversion step at home); US FBAR if the foreign account exceeds $10k

method: Emigrant property transfer (移民财产转移)
eligibility: Emigrated from the mainland with cancelled hukou; property evidence; SAFE approval at former hukou location
pros: Large amounts in one approved lump sum or staged per approval; staging no longer mandatory (2014)
cons: Requires SAFE approval and documentation; a US citizen by birth without mainland hukou does not qualify
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Approval-based; no FX tax on approved transfer; US §988 gain measured on basis

eligibility: Foreigner eligible to hold mainland property (residence permit / permanent residence ID; city rules)
pros: Purchases with FX settlement per PBOC [2006] No.3; sale proceeds can be repatriated
cons: City eligibility rules; property-cycle risk; not a pure conversion route
conversion_penalty_anatomy: PBOC [2006] No.3 arts. 7/13/22/32/37; PRC IIT on rental/transfer income

method: Foreign permanent resident ID salary FX
eligibility: Holds Foreign Permanent Resident ID (PRC) and mainland employment
pros: Documented salary FX purchase; convenience amount available
cons: Only for those holding the PRC permanent resident ID; tax record required above the convenience amount
conversion_penalty_anatomy: PRC IIT on salary; US §988/FEIE interplay; FBAR/8938

eligibility: Foreign passport holder employed in China; PRC IIT on the salary
pros: Salary FX purchase is not subject to the annual convenience amount when taxed
cons: Requires employment and tax payment; authenticity review
conversion_penalty_anatomy: PRC IIT withheld; US tax on wages (FEIE may apply); §988 on conversion

eligibility: Employer processes salary remittance through a payroll provider
pros: Handles documentation; net salary arrives in USD
cons: Requires employer cooperation; provider fees not published officially (blank)
conversion_penalty_anatomy: PRC IIT withheld; provider/receiving-bank fees blank (unverified)

eligibility: Hold stocks/bonds/funds or interest-bearing deposits in own name
pros: Dividends/interest already CNY; settle per rules
cons: Stock dividends subject to PRC IIT 20%; deposit interest IIT-exempt since 2008; treaty rate 10% may apply
conversion_penalty_anatomy: PRC withholding (20% individual / 10% treaty / deposit interest exempt); US §988; foreign tax credit possible

eligibility: Platform holds a SAFE-licensed payment-institution FX licence (汇发〔2019〕13号 scope)
pros: Digital, fast; current-account scope (shopping, study, travel)
cons: Scope is current-account business only; platform fees not published officially (blank)
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Platform partner-bank FX spread; fees blank (unverified)

eligibility: Real goods trade through a licensed platform with transaction records
pros: Legitimate trade settlement with FX purchase on evidence
cons: Requires real transactions; documentation heavy
conversion_penalty_anatomy: FX purchase on evidence; PRC trade taxes as applicable

eligibility: Any individual buying a QDII fund at a Chinese fund/bank
pros: USD exposure via institutional offshore investments; no personal approval
cons: Not a direct CNY-USD conversion; redemption returns CNY at market; fund fees blank (unverified)
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Fund-level fees blank; US tax on fund distributions as applicable

eligibility: GBA residents meeting WMC eligibility (2-year social insurance/tax or ¥400k income); ¥3M individual quota
pros: Closed-loop RMB 3M quota; invest in HK products via bank/securities channels
cons: GBA residency required; closed loop; not a direct cash conversion
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Product-level fees blank; FX via the closed loop

eligibility: Sold mainland property as a foreign individual; tax paid
pros: Large repatriation of sale proceeds per PBOC [2006] No.3 art. 7
cons: Property cycle; IIT on transfer; documentation heavy
conversion_penalty_anatomy: PRC IIT 20% on property transfer income; repatriation documentation

eligibility: CNY held in a PRC company account
pros: Clean corporate route with board resolution + tax filing
cons: >US$50,000 requires tax filing recordal (STA/SAFE No.40/19); audited financials for profit remittance
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Corporate tax filing; treaty dividend rate 10%

eligibility: PRC company with capital-account registration (内保外贷 / cross-border financing)
pros: Offshore funding without immediate conversion
cons: Capital-account registration required; funds use restricted; not an individual route
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Capital-account rules; penalties for misuse

eligibility: Former mainland employee (foreign passport holder) whose social insurance account is retained under MOHRSS Order No.16 art. 5
pros: Account balance can be paid out in a lump sum on written request to terminate the relationship
cons: Only for departed foreign employees; amount limited to the account balance
conversion_penalty_anatomy: Lump-sum payment is CNY; convert via M01; PRC tax treatment flagged
